name: AMETEK
description: AMETEK builds specialised electronic instruments and electromechanical parts that sit inside someone else's product or process: analyzers and sensors for factories, labs and power grids, flight-data and engine sensors for aircraft, precision motors and thermal systems, specialty metals and medical components. It sells mostly one-time instrument and component orders to equipment makers and plant operators, plus aftermarket spares, repairs and service (a stated aerospace MRO business). It grows largely by buying niche businesses (FARO Technologies in July 2025 and Kern Microtechnik in January 2025). Two segments, Electronic Instruments and Electromechanical, each earn high operating margins in niche markets.

businessLines.name: Electronic Instruments Group (EIG)
businessLines.how: Sells analytical, test, measurement and power instruments plus aerospace sensors and displays to process industries, labs, utilities and aircraft makers: one-time instrument sales, then spare parts, calibration, repair and (aerospace) MRO. Margin was 29.4 percent (30.7 percent in 2024), diluted by about 100 basis points from recent acquisitions.

businessLines.name: Electromechanical Group (EMG)
businessLines.how: Sells motion-control components (brushless motors, blowers, pumps), medical components and devices, specialty metals, electrical connectors and aircraft thermal-management systems, mostly as custom parts built into customers' equipment, plus aerospace MRO services. Top five customers are about 15 percent of EMG sales.

brands.name: FARO Technologies
brands.note: Acquired July 2025; 3D measurement and imaging (portable arms, laser scanners and trackers, software, service), reported in EIG. Total purchase price $1,023.7M (FARO and Kern together $1,136.7M).

brands.name: Kern Microtechnik
brands.note: Acquired January 2025; high-precision machining and optical inspection solutions. Purchase price $113.0M.
